title: Splice rollout lab notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick experimental notes for a "splice" style rollout (multiple tiny cohorts stitched together) instead of a single linear canary.
- Goal: validate model-variant + quantization combo under diverse client mixes while keeping global error rate < 0.5% and p95 latency budget intact.

High level idea (one line):
- Roll small, orthogonal cohorts (region x client-type x plan-tier) in parallel with ephemeral pins and fast-fallback hooks; monitor health signals and gradually expand by doubling cohort size or adding cohorts.

Cohort carving heuristics (practical rules):
- Primary axes: region, client-agent (mobile/desktop/server), customer-tier (free/paid/enterprise).
- Prefer cohorts that represent distinct cache and prefix distributions (e.g., server-to-server vs end-user chat).
- Keep any single cohort <= 0.25% of total qps for initial probe.
- Avoid putting enterprise customers in early cohorts unless explicitly opted-in.

Model/Variant strategy:
- Variant A: baseline full-precision v2.1 (control).
- Variant B: q4_0 quantized v2.1 (candidate) + small runtime kernel tweak.
- Variant C: distilled smaller model for heavy tails (fallback path).
- Pin semantics: can pin a cohort to a specific variant for 1–24h experiments; allow auto-unpin to revert to baseline if safety triggers hit.

Traffic routing and splice mechanics:
- Controller will create N cohorts (start with N=6) spread across regions.
- Use route key rules: if header X-Experiment: splice-2026 then cohort mapping -> variant.
- For SDK clients, prefer sticky cookie-based cohort assignment for 24h stability.
- For API customers, use deterministic hashing on customer_id + shard_key to maintain reproducibility.

Warmup and cache priming:
- Before expanding cohort, run warmup workload: 1000 synthetic prefix requests representative of target cohort distribution.
- Warmup should populate KV cache and prompt-cache for the model (target 60–90% cache hit rate measured via runtime metrics).
- Warmup endpoint: /internal/prime?cohort=xyz (auth token required).
- Don't count warmup traffic for billing/alerts; mark with header X-Internal-Warmup: true.

Observability checklist (queries to run in first 30m):
- Error rate by variant and region (5m windows): errors/token > 0.5% -> fail fast.
- P95 and p99 latency delta vs baseline: > +60ms at p95 OR +120ms at p99 -> alarm.
- Model quality smoke: run 50 synthetic golden prompts -> BLEU-like / exact-match thresholds, but keep lightweight (latency constraints).
- Cost delta per token (runtime metric): if candidate > 1.5x baseline -> rethink quantization config.
- Deployment signals: OOMs, kernel retries, queueing length spikes.

Health gates and automatic actions:
- Gate 1 (immediate): if 5m error rate > 0.5% for cohort -> rollback cohort only.
- Gate 2 (escalation): if 15m p95 increase > 60ms AND impacted qps > 10rps -> expand rollback to region.
- Gate 3 (global): if multiple regions hit Gate 2 within 30m -> global rollback and page on-call SRE.
- Fast-fallback: route traffic from candidate -> Variant C (smaller model) for 10m while rollback verifies.

Manual checklist for expansion (human-in-the-loop):
- Confirm warmup hit-rate metrics present and stable.
- Hand-run 5 golden prompts via remote-exec to check quality.
- Verify no increase in queueing or GPU memory pressure.
- Signal to support channel: #rollouts (brief note with cohort id and expansion time).

Coordination / communication plan:
- Pre-rollout: 1h sync with on-call SRE (ephemeral), release manager, and 1 eng owner.
- Post-expansion: 15m check-in messages every 15m for first hour in #rollouts.
- If rollback: run postmortem draft within 48h and capture live artifacts.

Edge cases and tricky stuff:
- Long-tail prefix churn: if cohort shows low cache hit and higher latency, don't expand; instead test targeted prefix caching or prompt rewriting.
- SDK clients with old versions: may not send experiment header; ensure deterministic hashing fallback is safe.
- Regional burst overlap: if two cohorts in adjacent regions cause a spike on shared infra (e.g., model shard), temporarily pause one cohort.

Open questions / experiments to try later:
- Variant sticky-window tuning: should cohort stick for 24h or 1h? pros/cons for user experience vs telemetry signal.
- Automatic cohort stitching heuristic: instead of manual doubling, use Bayesian bandit to allocate traffic to best-performing cohorts.
- Simulate workload mix with locally recorded traffic trace replay before rollout expansion.

Quick runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Rollback single cohort: API call -> POST /internal/rollout/rollback {cohort_id} (auth)
- Swap candidate to fallback: PATCH /internal/route {cohort_id, target: "variant-c"}
- Drain cohort: set cohort weight to 0, wait 60s, then unpin.

Todo (short):
- [ ] Add scripted warmup generator for mobile vs server prefixes (Ethan)
- [ ] Add dashboard tile for cohort-level cache-hit-rate (observability)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note template for enterprise customers in case of impact
- [ ] Run a simulated splice in staging with synthetic traffic trace (Max)

Notes to self: keep cohorts small, keep warmup cheap, prefer quality smoke over noisy metrics early, and always have a quick fallback to smaller model.

Last experiments run (log):
- 2025-12-02: quick splice across us-west/us-east with 3 cohorts -> cache warming improved p95 by 10ms, no regressions.
- 2026-01-14: attempted q4_0 + kernel tweak on us-west-only (cohort=3) -> small p99 spike due to kernel retry bug; rolled back and opened GH PR #2897.

References and snippets (copy these into scripts before kickoff):
- Warmup curl example: curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'X-Internal-Warmup: true' "https://api.redwood.local/internal/prime?cohort=splice-2026-01" -d @warmup_payload.json
- Health query (prom): sum(rate(runtime_errors_total{cohort=~"splice-.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{cohort=~"splice-.*"}[5m]))

End of lab notes.
